prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website redesign direction comp for a product decision board
Primary request: Design exactly one polished first-viewport landing page direction for Portal titled internally "THE OPTICAL SWITCHBOARD", drawing from precision optical benches, lens calibration plates, and laboratory-grade industrial instruments. This must look like an implementable desktop web interface, not concept art, and must avoid the familiar split-column SaaS hero.
Input image: the supplied Portal logo is a fixed brand reference. Reproduce that existing fractured violet aperture mark faithfully and do not redesign it.
Scene/backdrop: A warm off-white #eeede9 editorial canvas with a dark #17171a precision-instrument shell, disciplined violet accents #7c3aed and #b9a4ff, and restrained optical blue #5367a5. Use asymmetric but resolved website composition, generous space, practical top navigation, and enough of the next section visible below the fold to demonstrate the visual system.
Subject and layout: Header with the real Portal logo and exact wordmark text "Portal" at upper left, practical route navigation, and an unmistakable primary download action. The hero centers on a wide 2.39:1 product-film stage intended for the real 20-second showcase video. Present this stage as calibrated glass mounted on an optical bench, never inside a laptop, monitor, phone, browser window, or fake browser chrome. Within the film stage, show only an abstract neutral Portal desktop-widget silhouette with three restrained service labels: "ChatGPT", "Claude", "Gemini"; do not fabricate chat messages. Make Portal's mechanism immediately understandable: official AI services gathered in one floating desktop view. Integrate one large tactile violet aperture/service selector beside or partially overlapping the calibrated glass stage, with fine engraved ticks and clear connection to those three services. Place the exact hero copy "Your AI chats, one click away." prominently. Provide two clear actions with exact labels "Download for Windows" and "Download for macOS", with Windows unmistakably primary. Show a thin slice of a following section at the bottom using the same calibration-rail system, so the direction feels like a full website rather than a single poster.
Style/medium: pixel-perfect contemporary web UI mockup, realistic but restrained interface surfaces, distinctive precise industrial grotesk for headings and highly readable body/interface typography. Brushed aluminum edges, ground glass, engraved calibration ticks, crisp hairlines, small functional labels, subtle depth and believable web spacing. The presentation should feel premium, warm, engineered, and human rather than sterile or clinically complicated.
Composition/framing: landscape desktop viewport, straight-on screenshot-like view, 16:10 overall aspect, complete top navigation, complete hero, and 15–20% of the next section visible. Strong hierarchy and responsive intent should be visible through contained widths, adaptable columns, and touch-friendly button proportions. The large 2.39:1 film stage must be the central proof and primary visual anchor.
Text (verbatim and only these readable words): "Portal", "Your AI chats, one click away.", "Download for Windows", "Download for macOS", "ChatGPT", "Claude", "Gemini". Do not introduce any other readable copy, captions, metrics, route names, or labels; navigation may use minimal unlabeled precision controls so practical routing is visually apparent without extra words.
Constraints: preserve the supplied Portal logo design; primary action unmistakable; clear navigation affordances; central film stage is uncropped 2.39:1 and never placed in device mockup; enough next-section content to prove the system; UI mockup rather than art; exact copy spelling and capitalization.
Avoid: clinical complexity, standard split SaaS hero, generic purple glow blobs, bento grid, fake browser chrome, laptop/device mockups, fabricated chat messages, testimonials, metrics, press logos, customer claims, stock photography, excessive gradients, excessive glassmorphism, illegible microcopy, visual clutter, or watermark.
